Which investigation BEST turns the flaky signal into a reproducible causal test before accepting a code change?

options.text: Correlate import commit and query events, force the suspected interleaving with the scheduler, then verify an explicit completion dependency prevents that failing order.
options.why: This creates a falsifiable race hypothesis and checks a repair against the contract, rather than allowing timing luck to define success.

options.text: Delete the flaky assertion while keeping the background import unchanged, because an intermittent failure cannot support a reproducible regression test.
options.why: The controlled scheduler offers a way to reproduce the order deterministically, so removing the assertion would discard useful evidence before testing the hypothesis.

options.text: Increase the timeout on every integration test and treat fewer failures as proof that this index's specific import-completion race has been removed.
options.why: Global timeout changes can alter symptoms without establishing the missing dependency or demonstrating why the originally failing interleaving is impossible.

options.text: Keep unlimited retries and close the bug when the final attempt passes, assuming eventual index visibility proves the first query satisfied the completion contract.
options.why: A later successful query does not establish that the initial query waited for commit, so retries can hide the exact ordering defect under investigation.

questions.decision: Use the controlled scheduler to reproduce the missing completion dependency, then enforce the contract and retain a test that fails without that synchronization. Retries may help characterize timing, but a later pass does not identify the cause. The source lesson becomes concrete here through event ordering and a regression check tied to the required commit-before-query behavior.

video_evidence.concept: Reproduce intermittent failure, identify its root cause, and verify a causal repair rather than hiding it behind retries.

drills.title: Preserve the intended boundary
drills.stem: Judge each proposal independently against the stated requirement. These supplemental exercises are unscored; there is no fixed number of Yes answers.

rows.text: Requirement: diagnostic agents cannot update assets. Proposal: a read-named wrapper forwards arbitrary paths using a repair-capable credential.
rows.why: The reachable upstream write path remains available despite the tool name.

rows.text: Requirement: a missing sample must not mean clean. Proposal: typed missing states are excluded from numeric aggregation and disclosed in the report.
rows.why: The application preserves the distinction between absent evidence and measured zero.

rows.text: Requirement: at most three reminders per rolling hour. Proposal: concurrent workers reserve recipient quota atomically at the send boundary.
rows.why: Atomic reservation prevents workers from spending the same remaining allowance.

rows.text: Requirement: the current rule governs historical examples. Proposal: examples keep effective-edition labels and are explicitly identified as illustrations.
rows.why: The template separates illustrative evidence from current governing instructions.

rows.text: Requirement: only eligible rooms are recommended. Proposal: semantic relevance determines eligibility despite contradictory capacity fields.
rows.why: Similarity cannot override authoritative hard predicates.

drills.title: What does the measurement establish?
drills.stem: Decide whether each conclusion follows from the given facts. Judge rows independently; these are supplemental unscored exercises.

rows.text: A worker is read-only because no write appeared in one happy-path run, although its configuration inherits the parent tools.
rows.why: Observed nonuse does not establish that the write capability is unavailable.

rows.text: A request starts four minutes after the last cache read of an identical eligible prefix. Under the default five-minute rule, that read can refresh the entry.
rows.why: Qualifying reads refresh lifetime from their request start.

rows.text: A batch has 80,000 requests and 300 MB of serialized content. It satisfies limits of 100,000 requests or 256 MB, whichever comes first.
rows.why: Its serialized size exceeds the independent byte ceiling.

rows.text: Discarding every order-inconsistent judge result can change the assessed population when inconsistency concentrates on difficult cases.
rows.why: The retained subset may differ systematically from the full workload.

rows.text: A 50% inference-spend reduction proves the same percentage reduction in total operating expense when review cost is unmeasured.
rows.why: The measured category does not establish how other costs changed.

drills.title: Choose the diagnostic boundary
drills.stem: Match each observed issue to its BEST initial diagnostic boundary. Choices may repeat; judge each row independently.

rows.text: Accented place names exceed the radio payload byte cap despite staying under its character cap.
rows.why: The serialized outgoing artifact violates the channel contract.

rows.text: The catalogue is current, but seat recommendations use yesterday's availability.
rows.why: The changing operational fact needs its own authoritative request-time source.

rows.text: A pairwise judge changes its preferred candidate when presentation order is reversed.
rows.why: Counterbalancing and explicit inconsistent-case treatment address the measurement bias.

rows.text: A diagnostic wrapper can reach a repair endpoint through an arbitrary path parameter.
rows.why: The exposed operation and credential need an enforceable role boundary.

rows.text: The cited standard is real but belongs to a later edition than the question asks about.
rows.why: Evidence selection must match the requested applicability period before generation.
